questions.markdown:
Given:

$$
I_0 = 1\,pA \text{ at } 20^\circ C
$$

Find:

$$
I_D = ? \quad \text{at } 150^\circ C,\ V_D = 0.5V
$$

$$
r_d = ? \quad \text{at } 150^\circ C
$$

$$
I_0' = I_0\,2^{\frac{150-20}{10}}
$$

$$
I_0' = 1p\cdot 2^{13}
$$

$$
I_0' = 8.192\,nA
$$

$$
V_T = \frac{T}{11600} = \frac{150+273}{11600} = \frac{423}{11600} = 36.465\,mV
$$

$$
I_D = I_0'\left[e^{\frac{V_D}{\eta V_T}} - 1\right]
$$

Assume diode is Ge, $\eta = 1$

$$
I_D = 8.192n\left[e^{\frac{0.5\times11600}{423}} - 1\right]
$$

$$
I_D = 7.383\,mA
$$

$$
r_d = \frac{\eta V_T}{I_0' + I_D} = \frac{1\times36.465m}{8.192n + 7.383m} = 4.939\,\Omega
$$

Assume diode is Si, $\eta = 2$

$$
I_D = 8.192n\left[e^{\frac{0.5\times11600}{2\times423}} - 1\right]
$$

$$
I_D = 7.168\,\mu A
$$

$$
r_d = \frac{2\times423}{(8.192n + 7.168\mu)\times11600} = 9.378\,k\Omega
$$

**NOTE:** Based on the decimal points taken, diode current and resistance can vary. Please consider the diode current and resistance values with $\pm (10 \text{ to } 15)\%$ tolerance while evaluating the answer scripts.
